name: Compound Growth
description: Project a starting value forward across several periods of compounding growth.
formula: Ending value = Starting value × (1 + Growth rate) ^ Number of periods
business_contexts: a company projecting revenue forward at a compounding annual growth rate
an investor projecting a portfolio's value forward at a compounding return
a city projecting population forward at a compounding growth rate
a startup projecting its user base forward at a compounding growth rate
a bank projecting a compounding balance forward across several years
question_patterns: Given the starting value, growth rate, and number of periods below, what is the ending value under compound growth?
Calculate the ending value after compounding the growth rate below across the periods shown.
What value results from compounding the starting value below at the growth rate given, across the periods shown?
Calculate the compounded ending value using the figures below.
Using the figures given, project the starting value forward under compound growth.
solution_logic: Step 1: Calculate ending value = starting_value × (1 + growth_rate) ^ periods
key_insight: Compound growth applies the rate to the already-grown value each period, unlike simple growth — the gap between the two widens with every additional period.
common_mistakes: Applying the growth rate as simple growth (rate × periods) instead of raising (1 + rate) to the power of periods
Forgetting that the exponent is the number of periods, not the growth rate
framework_soundbite: Compound growth raises (1 + rate) to the power of the periods — each period grows off the last, not off the original base.
